## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The supplied code diagnoses item embeddings and positive-versus-negative scores through a model view. The HSTU backbone implementation is absent, so its internal representation computation cannot be verified. `log2feats(sequence)` supplies per-position sequence features; `predict_score(features, items)` converts those features into candidate logits. The probe scores all valid training positions rather than selecting a final user representation. Any final readout elsewhere must use the final nonpadding position for left-padded histories.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the view and its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`; the latter two are unused. It accesses `view.item_emb.weight` and `view.model.itemnum` to select real-item embeddings, excluding padding and reserved tokens.

The loader yields `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with tensors shaped `B × L`. For up to ten batches, the probe switches to evaluation mode, computes sequence features without gradients, stacks positive and negative IDs into `B × L × 2`, and scores them together. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Samples up to 2,048 item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result through `(mean_cosine + 1) / 2`. Higher values indicate stronger directional alignment; approximately 0.5 corresponds to mean cosine zero.
- **Score margins:** Computes `positive_logit − negative_logit`. Higher mean and tenth-percentile margins indicate clearer separation. Lower negative-beats-positive and margin-below-0.5 rates indicate fewer ranking errors and weak separations.
- **Category breakdown:** Counts metadata category occurrences separately for positive and negative items in low-margin and wrong-rank cases, retaining the top twenty categories.

# Perturbation & Tests

There are no sequence shuffles, masking interventions, sensitivity tests, or gradient probes. Random embedding subsampling controls computation; sampled negatives provide the score comparisons.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, covering collapse, four margin statistics, and nested category counts. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into instructions requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; it does not itself generate that interpretation.

These are training-sample diagnostics, not validation HR@10 or full-catalog quality measurements. Margins depend on logit scale and negative sampling. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists will normally be empty. Missing valid positions produce zero-valued margin defaults, which must not be interpreted as measured health.

[Measuring Recency Bias (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) also cautions that excessive emphasis on recent items can hurt recommendation performance. These findings motivate measuring both recency dependence and ranking stability, without assuming greater sensitivity is better.

A proposed HSTU diagnostic: keep the trained model and candidate sets fixed; compare unchanged histories with recent-window truncation, valid-item shuffling, and removal of a coherent recent activity block identified from available timestamps or item text. ## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The supplied code diagnoses item embeddings and positive-versus-negative scores through a model view. The HSTU backbone implementation is absent, so its internal representation computation cannot be verified. `log2feats(sequence)` supplies per-position sequence features; `predict_score(features, items)` converts those features into candidate logits. The probe scores all valid training positions rather than selecting a final user representation. Any final readout elsewhere must use the final nonpadding position for left-padded histories.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the view and its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`; the latter two are unused. It accesses `view.item_emb.weight` and `view.model.itemnum` to select real-item embeddings, excluding padding and reserved tokens.

The loader yields `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with tensors shaped `B × L`. For up to ten batches, the probe switches to evaluation mode, computes sequence features without gradients, stacks positive and negative IDs into `B × L × 2`, and scores them together. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Samples up to 2,048 item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result through `(mean_cosine + 1) / 2`. Higher values indicate stronger directional alignment; approximately 0.5 corresponds to mean cosine zero.
- **Score margins:** Computes `positive_logit − negative_logit`. Higher mean and tenth-percentile margins indicate clearer separation. Lower negative-beats-positive and margin-below-0.5 rates indicate fewer ranking errors and weak separations.
- **Category breakdown:** Counts metadata category occurrences separately for positive and negative items in low-margin and wrong-rank cases, retaining the top twenty categories.

# Perturbation & Tests

There are no sequence shuffles, masking interventions, sensitivity tests, or gradient probes. Random embedding subsampling controls computation; sampled negatives provide the score comparisons.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, covering collapse, four margin statistics, and nested category counts. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into instructions requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; it does not itself generate that interpretation.

These are training-sample diagnostics, not validation HR@10 or full-catalog quality measurements. Margins depend on logit scale and negative sampling. Category metadata is unavailable in this task, so category lists will normally be empty. Missing valid positions produce zero-valued margin defaults, which must not be interpreted as measured health.
